newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Historic Brazilian city seeks UNESCO flood help.
newsitem.headline: Historic Brazilian city seeks UNESCO flood help.

text.p: Brazil's historic city of Ouro Preto has asked the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) to help it cope with damage caused by torrential rain, officials said on Wednesday.

Deputy mayor Renan de Moraes told Reuters by telephone Ouro Preto did not have the architectural expertise to evaluate the impact of six days of rain and floods on its colonial buildings. "We hope UNESCO will send a team out to help us evaluate the damage. We're not asking for money just yet," he said.

Ouro Preto, founded in 1698 and the jewel in the crown of Brazil's architectural heritage, was one of 125 cities in Minas Gerais state lashed by heavy rains. At least 71 people died and tens of thousands were left homeless in Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro state. "The damage is great," de Moraes said.

Ouro Preto, named after the rich gold finds that made it one of Brazil's wealthiest cities in the 1700s, was placed on UNESCO's World Heritage list in 1985. An official at the city's Tourism Secretariat told Reuters he did not think flood damage to historic buildings had been that bad but it was impossible to tell without expert help from UNESCO.

The rains began to subside on Wednesday but rivers remained swollen and thousands of people were still stranded, local media reported. Health authorities have launched a campaign to prevent outbreaks of disease, in particular leptospirosis, transmitted by rat urine, which causes fever, jaundice and internal bleeding.
